It is a spacious and pleasant cafe located on the first floor of COEX in Samseong-dong. Coffee and desserts such as tiramisu are especially popular. We summarize the main reviews below.
space and atmosphere
• The interior of the store is spacious and has many seats, so you don’t have to worry about finding a seat. There are a variety of seats available, including sofa seats and group seats, so you can chat or relax comfortably.
• The interior has a simple and luxurious feel with a Japanese touch. Many people say that it is comfortable because the lighting is bright and the feeling of openness is good.
• Some seats may require eye contact with the person across from you, but overall, it is a good space to sit and chat for a long time.
Representative menu and taste
• Tiramisu: There are many types, including Earl Gray, matcha, original, and seasonal. Earl Gray tiramisu and matcha tiramisu are especially popular. Tiramisu is large in size, has a rich taste, and many say it goes well with coffee.
• Coffee: Characterized by a mild taste with a hint of acidity. There is a variety of coffee menus including Americano, Latte, and Cortado, and a decaffeinated option is also available.
• Special drinks such as salted cream coffee granita are also available. Recommended for those who prefer a less bitter, richer taste of coffee.
• Desserts such as cookies: Cookies are also said to be good value for money.
Price range and more
• The prices of drinks and desserts are somewhat higher than those of regular cafes (Americano 4,900 won, tiramisu 8,000-9,000 won, etc.).
• Pets are allowed, parking is paid (3,000 won for 30 minutes).
• Many people say that the staff's response is friendly.

Recommended Points
• Perfect for when you want to enjoy spacious seats, a pleasant atmosphere, and delicious tiramisu and coffee at COEX.
• Both desserts and coffee are guaranteed to be of a certain level of quality, and are also suitable as a place for conversation, relaxation, or meetings.
What's disappointing
• The price may seem a bit high.
• Some seats may lack privacy.
Overall review
Gabaedo in Samseong-dong is a cafe with a wide space, a bright and luxurious atmosphere, and a variety of tiramisu and sour coffee. This is a recommended place if you want to enjoy dessert and coffee comfortably without worrying about your seat at COEX.

It's on the first floor of COEX, so the ceiling is high and there are plenty of seats.

Winter Dream, Green Angel, etc...

reviews.text:
Originally, Korean beer tasted completely old, so I always drink imported beer. When I visited Homeboy Seoul in Yeonnam-dong, I ordered Jeju Wheat Ale on the menu and it had the feel of craft beer, so I thought that Korean craft beer was also good. After that, Korean craft beer gradually became better and I was following Jeju Beer on Instagram. A few weeks ago, I posted on Instagram that there was a whiskey oak barrel from Highland Park, a 220-year-old whiskey brand. I saw a post about a limited edition that was released only once called Jeju Beer's Imperial Stout, so I was curious and applied for a bottle, and today was the day to pick up the limited edition beer I applied for.

The place I designated as the place where I could pick up Jeju Beer Imperial Stout Edition was the Living Beer Samsung COEX branch, so I stopped by.

I didn't even know a store like this existed, but I first found out about it through a Jeju beer event. When I said I was there to pick up beer, they checked my name and reservation text and handed me some chocolate that they said would be good to pair with limited edition beer.

When I showed the reservation text message, I saw that I could get a 20% discount if I ordered a snack when I visited to pick up the beer. I was wondering if the fried chicken was good and there was a lot of fried chicken on the menu, so I wanted to use the 20% discount chance. I was curious so I asked what the representative menu was, and they said Angry Birds Drag and asked me to pack it with the bone.

As I looked around the store while the fried chicken was being fried, I realized that Living Beer was a store that sold Korean brand craft beer, so if I liked fried chicken, I might stop by more often.

About 10 minutes later, the well-packaged Angry Birds were ready, and when I got home and unfolded them, the visuals didn't feel any different from those at a typical franchise chicken restaurant, but the volume didn't seem to be sparse or anything, and the chunks seemed chunky in their own way.

There was a seasoning sauce included, but I don't really like seasoning sauce, so I just tasted the fried chicken as is. It was spicy because there was spicy seasoning spread between the skin and the flesh, not the batter, so it tasted and felt similar to Popeyes or KFC's Hot & Krispy Chicken. When I ordered, I saw Angry Bird Red on the menu, so I thought Angry Bird tasted like the original chicken, so I ordered it. Although the spiciness is not a big deal for adults, it was good for young family members. As I was eating it, I said I couldn't eat it because it was spicy, so I looked at the photo of the menu again and found that the English menu under Angry Birds was Spicy Fried Chicken, and Angry Birds Red was spicier.

In conclusion, I ordered and tasted the Angry Birds, the restaurant's signature dish, while stopping by to pick up a limited edition beer. The chicken itself was juicy and tasted good, but I didn't feel that it was different from the commonly seen major chicken brands in Korea. I don't really like chicken from those brands, and I prefer KFC original chicken or old-fashioned chicken like yellow whole chicken or Duduul chicken. It was a visit that made me feel like I wouldn't come back to eat the chicken.

“The suffering of dry chicken”

These days, I'm having fun trying local chicken restaurants at their stores...

In the past, I thought this place used to barbecue chicken on a grill with a window visible from the outside, but at some point it changed to oven-roasting.
They also run a Korean buffet during the day.
I don't know if it's a shared kitchen or if it's a direct business, but it's also a place that's making various changes to survive.

The menu I ordered was grilled salt and braised pork belly.

The starting conditions are mediocre and poor compared to any of the competitors.
